rules.observation: Repeated prefill.decode_interval with waiting_requests>0 or chunk_pending=1, while per-rank prefill service is insufficient.
rules.diagnosis: The configured decode interval explicitly prevents the admission scan. Free KV or absent budget-gate events do not rule this out.
alternatives: Queued requests may also be ineligible for cache transfer or capacity.
Another DP rank can arm the interval; local queue pressure may differ.
rules.check: Correlate rank-local gate windows with queue slope, prefill effective-token rates, decode output rate and resolved cadence. Event counts do not measure wait time.
rules.action: Test interval24 ->12 at fixed topology, concurrency, token/request caps and cache warmup.
rules.expected: Fewer consecutive deferrals and higher prefill service; decode ITL may worsen.
rules.reject_if: Output throughput or p10 user speed regresses without a useful Pareto tradeoff; gate evidence does not clear.
rules.status: CPU behavior verified; GPU effect pending

rules.observation: Queued work with input/chunk budget encounters and available KV; explicit interval and request caps are not the dominant obstruction.
rules.diagnosis: The admission compute budget limits prefill batch formation.
alternatives: Replay rows consume the same budget.
DP divides declared chunk size.
Post-admission checks are not rejected requests.
rules.check: Read tuning_scheduler_config per rank and admitted extend/replay rows; separate input budget from chunk budget and workspace limits.
rules.action: Change only the binding effective token cap within verified workspace limits; keep the other cap fixed.
rules.expected: Larger useful admitted batches and increased prefill service, potentially worse TTFT/ITL.
rules.reject_if: Service does not improve, memory guard trips, or long-context coverage/errors worsen.

rules.observation: Request-slot encounters and a growing queue while device capacity remains available.
rules.diagnosis: Request rows may constrain admission before KV capacity is exhausted.
alternatives: An earlier gate can hide a later memory limit.
Increasing active rows can exceed decode graph capture coverage.
rules.check: Compare resolved per-rank row limit with running requests and graph-use metrics; inspect FULL/SWA separately.
rules.action: Raise only the binding per-rank admission cap in a bounded trial; account for graph and request-pool memory.
rules.expected: More active work, if another gate does not replace this one.
rules.reject_if: KV gates/retractions immediately replace the row gate or latency worsens without useful throughput.

rules.observation: FULL/SWA/shared-capacity failures during queued work, or retractions under sustained load.
rules.diagnosis: The effective device-pool geometry or reservations cannot fit the workload.
alternatives: Locked prefixes and future output reservation differ from physical usage.
Graph buffers, draft state and replay tails consume memory.
Wrapper memory_budget can duplicate a lower-level gate.
rules.check: Compare startup actual capacities, per-pool evictable/available tokens and reservation observations. Do not add wrapper and allocator events.
rules.action: Choose one evidenced intervention: modest static-memory increase if proven headroom, or lower active-request/reservation pressure; never infer memory from the flag alone.
rules.expected: Capacity gate clears without OOM/retraction or excessive recomputation.
rules.reject_if: Measured capacity does not change or another physical pool still binds.

rules.observation: Eager dispatch grows under high active batch sizes despite a configured decode graph runner.
rules.diagnosis: Decode/verify graph coverage may be insufficient, but the eager counter also includes prefill and idle paths.
alternatives: Prefill is deliberately eager in the baseline.
Target versus draft and graph eligibility predicates differ.
A runner receipt does not prove every layer replayed.
rules.check: Use existing CUDA graph counters with producer-defined labels and actual phase context; obtain mode-specific dispatch evidence before attributing eager events to decode.
rules.action: Only after confirming uncovered decode/verify sizes, test a larger capture cap with the actual KV-memory cost recorded.
rules.expected: Increased relevant graph use and lower exposed host overhead.
rules.reject_if: Extra captures shrink KV enough to harm reuse or relevant graph use does not rise.
rules.status: Ambiguous signal: do not auto-change from aggregate eager counts

rules.observation: Uneven per-rank queue and cache reuse, or idle serving capacity with few arrivals despite active client work.
rules.diagnosis: Router affinity, CPU request handling or client supply may limit useful GPU work.
alternatives: Workload trace lengths differ by lane.
Queue depletion can be caused by a slow upstream stage.
Router prefix approximation differs from server radix-cache state.
rules.check: Inspect the deployed router implementation, routing headers, client offered load, HTTP activity, per-rank arrivals and tier hit rates.
rules.action: Correct missing baseline session routing first. Tune frontend workers or routing only after distinguishing supply starvation from affinity overload.
rules.expected: More balanced useful arrivals without destroying cache locality.
rules.reject_if: GPU batches merely reshuffle while cache misses or end-to-end latency rise.

rules.observation: Host-table startup shows lower huge-page coverage on some ranks, optionally with MADV_COLLAPSE errno12.
rules.diagnosis: Actual table backing differs despite identical layout settings; address translation and placement may confound rank latency.
alternatives: Concurrent snapshot persistence/checksum or loader reads repopulate file cache.
NUMA-local contiguous memory or process affinity differs.
The workload may not expose host lookups enough for coverage to matter.
rules.check: Read per-layer/rank coverage, /proc scheduler affinity and NUMA placement, host/cgroup headroom and staging completion. Correlate with matched-rank forward latency before attribution.
rules.action: First start a fresh deployment after staging/checksum I/O completes, holding server configuration fixed. Change binding/layout only if placement evidence supports a separate controlled trial.
rules.expected: If temporary staging pressure caused the backing skew, coverage may improve without a serving-config change.
rules.reject_if: Coverage stays skewed or improves without a latency benefit; do not claim a scheduler bottleneck or host-lookup speedup from the receipt alone.
rules.status: Startup backing skew observed; causal performance effect unverified
runtime_evidence: native-r0 server.log at2026-10-22T17:28:33Z..17:28:35Z: layer14 rank2=30%, rank3=32%, ranks0/1=100%; immutable snapshot persistence still active.

rules.observation: Decoder tail graph capture receipts while whole-prefill cuda_graph mode is prefill_none, with early warmup service variation.
rules.diagnosis: Layer-tail graphs are enabled independently of whole-prefill graph dispatch and capture lazily. Cold capture overhead is part of this window.
alternatives: Cold prefix misses require real prefill work. Client reconstruction, request arrival skew and host-table backing can also alter early rates.
rules.check: Read capture timestamps/cumulative seconds and client phase together with per-rank useful prefill counters. Whole-forward none does not imply all layers are eager.
rules.action: Let canonical warmup progress before ranking steady-state rates. If tail coverage remains a hypothesis, obtain bounded replay/fallback counters before changing MAX_ROWS; keep MIN_PREFILL_TOKENS semantics separate.
rules.expected: Cold capture receipts taper as shapes are covered; steady-state benefit requires paired evidence.
rules.reject_if: Capture continues for new shapes, or useful rates do not stabilize; no conclusion from gate counts alone.
rules.status: Observed in baseline-r1 canonical warmup; causal performance effect untested
runtime_evidence: baseline-r1 server.log 2026-10-22 11:02:50–11:03:00 Pacific: TP0 capture receipts despite prefill backend disabled.

policy.units: Keep rank/process labels; encounter counts are not unique requests, wait seconds or fallback percentages.
policy.window: Require repeated consistent live windows and workload-phase context; cold/warmup observations cannot certify Pareto throughput.
policy.early_stop: Safety/invalidity stops immediately; clear sustained diagnostic evidence can stop a screen, whose partial throughput stays exploratory.
policy.promotion: Paired equal-duration screens with full corpus/canonical warmup, then full-duration validity, latency and refreshed frontier checks.
policy.unknown: Missing producers/events are unknown, not zero; add discriminating instrumentation when alternatives remain.
